The rest of the buffet’s food selection left me underwhelmed. While there were classics like sushi, prime rib, and a decent salad bar, the quality felt unremarkable for the price. The sushi, for example, was fresh but lacked the bold seasoning and artistry I’ve seen at other strip buffets. The prime rib was overly seasoned with salt, masking the meat’s natural flavor. Even the salad bar offered only basic options, with no creative dressings or add-ons to elevate it. For a hotel that markets itself as a “premium” dining destination, these dishes felt more like afterthoughts than standout experiences.  

The lack of communication from staff about the buffet’s limitations was frustrating. If the pasta station is occasionally closed or reserved for VIP guests, there should be clear signage or staff alerts to avoid false hope. Similarly, the sandwich bar’s omission of bread—a basic necessity—seemed like a glaring oversight. I overheard multiple guests expressing the same confusion, which suggests this is a recurring issue rather than an isolated mistake. It’s hard to trust a hotel’s branding when these details are so inconsistent.  

That said, the desserts genuinely impressed. The chocolate fountain with fresh strawberries and house-made truffles was worth the splurge, and the interactive dessert station (with a chef drizzling caramel and lighting desserts on fire) added a fun, Instagram-worthy touch. I even tried the “molecular gastronomy” dessert—though I’ll admit the experience was more novelty than flavor—but it was enough to make me overlook some of the earlier disappointments.  

If I had to compare this buffet to others on the strip, it still lags behind. The [insert competitor’s name] offers a similar price point

"Each dish was a hit, especially the kid-friendly options. The staff went above and beyond to make us feel welcome. Can’t wait to bring the family back for another fantastic experience!"  

(31 words)

The attention to detail and personalized care at Shine Salon set it apart. Charlton’s expertise and friendly staff created a welcoming atmosphere where I felt truly valued. The price-to-quality ratio is unbeatable—no hidden fees or upsells, just exceptional results. Every strand of my hair feels intentional, and the color is vibrant yet natural. The wait time was worth it, as Charlton prioritized perfection over speed. I’m also impressed by the follow-up care, like the text checking if I’m happy with the outcome. It’s rare to find a salon that blends professionalism with genuine warmth. Shine Salon isn’t just a service—it’s an investment in confidence. I’ll keep referring friends and returning for every cut, color, and style. The quality and results speak for themselves! (102 words)

The bar fight was a lively, interactive twist on tasting menus—our table cheered as the Blackened Shrimp Lumpia’s smoky, citrusy kick paired flawlessly with Mr. Pineapple’s tropical hoppiness, giving it a clear win. The Monkfish Taco, while flavorful, felt let down by its greasy coating; we’ll test the grilled version another visit. The spring salad, though, was a revelation—crisp greens, tangy vinaigrette, and unexpected textures that danced in harmony (oral orchestra indeed!). The vibe here is casual yet vibrant, with friendly servers who clearly love their craft beer. Perfect for date nights or groups craving inventive eats and a drink in a welcoming spot. Can’t wait to return!

Creative fusion of flavors—try sesame noodles in a burrito! Tons of fresh options; build your perfect dish. Service is friendly, portions generous. A fun twist on comfort food that feels new every visit! The Glendale location is cozy, making it a top spot for innovative, flavorful meals!

The service didn’t help matters—our server seemed disengaged, offering minimal guidance and leaving us to fumble through the menu. For a splurge-worthy spot, the lack of standout elements is baffling. The drinks? Overpriced cocktails with no signature flair. The ambiance, while undeniably sleek and masculine (think navy leather booths and yacht-club bric-a-brac), felt more trying-too-hard than inviting. We left feeling like we’d paid for a photo op, not a meal. Even the wine list leaned toward generic bottles that didn’t elevate the experience. In a city brimming with better options—places where quality justifies the price—STK comes off as a hollow imitation of luxury. Save your cash for a chef-driven spot with actual culinary ambition. Unless you’re there strictly for the “vibes,” which, honestly, wear thin after one underwhelming bite.

The Southern-style brunch menu is a standout, with perfectly flaky buttermilk biscuits and golden syrup drizzle. The coffee is bold and fresh, and the service is friendly and prompt. Every bite feels like a celebration of flavors—creamy, spicy, and sweet all in one. Can’t wait to return! (45 words)

The food truly stood out—every bite felt thoughtfully crafted. The bison burger was juicy and flavorful, paired perfectly with truffle fries that were crispy and indulgent. Even my partner’s salmon, roasted to perfection with a citrus glaze, impressed. The mac and cheese? A creamy, cheesy dream. Our server, *Jenna*, made excellent drink recommendations, and the table was refilled promptly. The space is cozy yet vibrant, with a mix of modern art and warm lighting that invites lingering. While the lunch crowd was lively, the noise never felt overwhelming. TMI’s attention to detail—from the fresh herbs on the plate to the locally brewed ale sample I’ll try next time—elevates the experience. This isn’t just a replacement for Lisa G’s; it’s a fresh gem. Can’t wait to return for dinner and see how the menu shines under new lights. (106 words)

Let’s talk about the seasoning, though. That Red Robin rub? It’s like the restaurant’s secret handshake with flavor. Sprinkle it on your burger, and suddenly your meat isn’t just meat—it’s a party in your mouth. I’d go as far as saying it’s the reason the Royal Red Robin transcends its “basic burger with an egg” premise. Plus, the chocolate milkshake? Oh, that’s a whole other level of indulgence. It’s thick, like drinking a milkshake made from chocolate mousse. I’ve had vanilla here too, and it’s so creamy it could probably qualify as a dessert. But here’s the thing: When you pair the shake with that burger and fries, you’re not just eating—you’re *experiencing*. You’re in a food coma zone by the time you reach your desk at 1:15 PM.  

And yes, let’s get back to those fries. Bottomless, golden, salty perfection. They’re not just for kids—though if you’ve got a small army of rugrats, this place is your brunch savior. Order a burger, and the kids can graze for hours without costing you a fortune. Meanwhile, you’re slathered in ketchup, happily mind-numbing your way through a second helping. I’ve seen people disappear entire baskets by themselves. They’re addictive in the same way potato chips are, except they’re longer and occasionally come with a side of regret (ketchup-smeared shirts and all).  

But here’s the real compromise: You walk in expecting a basic chain meal, but leave feeling like you scored a cheat-day victory. The lettuce is still a tragedy, but the egg? The seasoning? The shakes? Those fries? They’re the kind of “junk” that makes you forgive the small sins. I still take my lunch crew here, even if I end up stealing half their fries while pretending to make a “strategic move” to “share.” It’s not the healthiest lunch, but hey—at least I’m not at Chili’s.

The menu offered a nice mix of fresh, light options like grilled salmon and quinoa bowls, as well as heartier choices like the avocado-lime chicken, which was juicy and flavorful. The staff was attentive, even during a busy lunch rush, which added to the laid-back yet efficient vibe. While the lack of reusable tableware felt slightly outdated for a health-focused spot, the portions were generous and satisfying. For eco-conscious diners, suggesting a small fee for disposables could encourage sustainability without hassle. Though the absence of calorie counts might deter those tracking macros, the overall quality and price make this a solid pick for a guilt-free meal. I’ll definitely return and recommend it for its balance of taste, convenience, and mindful pricing.

"Service was friendly but a bit rushed due to the high turnout. The beer taps featured both local brews and some unique imports, which was a nice touch. While the crowd made it hard to grab a seat, the lively energy added to the fun. Would definitely return for the music and games, even if I have to wait for a spot." (53 words)

continued review:  
The overall experience with Reliable Repair has been nothing short of excellent. Everett’s expertise and dedication to ensuring the repair was thorough and long-lasting truly set this company apart. Beyond just fixing the microwave, he took the time to educate us on how to maintain our appliances, which gave us peace of mind about preventing future issues. His attention to detail—like pointing out the previous installation’s flaws—showed a level of professionalism I haven’t seen in other service providers.  

What impressed me most was Reliable Repair’s transparency. They clearly explained the repair process, costs, and timelines, which made the entire situation stress-free. While the waiting period for parts was a bit lengthy, the technician kept us informed every step of the way, and the final result justified the patience. The fact that Everett returned the next week to complete the repair with the new parts demonstrated a commitment to customer satisfaction.  

I also appreciated the company’s follow-up after the service. They asked if we were satisfied and even offered to assist with any other concerns, reinforcing their customer-centric approach. In an industry where rushed fixes and vague explanations are common, Reliable Repair’s integrity and craftsmanship are refreshing.  

If I had one suggestion, it would be for the scheduling system to allow more flexibility for busy homeowners, but I recognize that balancing technician availability with demand is a challenge. All in all, I wholeheartedly recommend Reliable Repair. Their combination of technical skill, clear communication, and genuine care for customers makes them a standout choice. If Everett’s ever in the area again, I’d trust him with all my appliances!

The food here is consistently hit-or-miss, which is why I dock a half star. For instance, the Tom Yum Shrimp soup is a revelation—zesty, aromatic, and perfectly balanced between spicy and sour—though on a few occasions, the shrimp felt a tad underseasoned. The garlic beef is always tender and packed with flavor, and the pad see ew’s smoky peanut sauce hits the spot, but the pad thai can be overly sweet, leaning into an almost cloying syrupiness that drowns out the dish’s more delicate flavors. Still, the variety of options is impressive; the menu offers both traditional and more adventurous choices, like the basil pork or the mango sticky rice, which is always a comforting, buttery finale.  

The pacing of service is a lingering issue. On a quiet afternoon, my server took nearly 15 minutes to take an order, and another time, the kitchen held a dish for 20 minutes because it “wasn’t ready.” While the staff is friendly and apologetic, the delays add up. That said, the cleanliness and brightness of the space can’t be ignored. The walls are painted in calming neutrals, and the dining area is spotless—unlike some Thai joints where the aroma of oregano-scented air freshener clings too heavily. Archi’s leans into subtle touches, like potted herbs on tables and Thai music playing faintly in the background.  

For the price, I’d still recommend it. The meal-to-cost ratio is unmatched, and the quality remains solid for a casual bite. While it’s not a “special occasion” spot, it’s a reliable, no-frills option for when you just need a quick hit of pad see ew and a soup that makes you sweat. If the staff can tighten up the timing, Archi’s could easily be a five-star staple. Until then, it’s a three-star with a side of hope.

The rest of the meal was a mixed bag of culinary curiosity and service missteps. While the Manchurian-inspired vegetable pakoras were a standout—crunchy, spiced with a smoky depth, and utterly memorable—the execution of the other dishes felt inconsistent. The red curry, though flavorful, leaned heavily on coconut milk and peanuts, straying further from Indian spices than I’d expect from a dish named “Indian style.” The Tom Yum, while inventive with its vegetable base, lacked the punchy heat and aromatic brightness that defines the classic. It was clear the kitchen aimed for bold experimentation, but the results often veered into confusion rather than brilliance.  

The real disappointment, though, lay in the interaction with the staff. The waiter’s defensiveness and the sneaky service charge felt like a betrayal of trust. It’s one thing to upsell or request a tip, but disguising a mandatory fee—especially after tax—felt like a calculated ploy. When he returned with the receipt, the $0 service charge line struck me as a transparent attempt to reclassify the fee, possibly to avoid tipping regulations. The fact that he then leaned on us for additional gratuity, smirking as he asked, “Was everything to your liking?” made it clear this wasn’t an oversight.  

I left the bill with an extra dollar as a sarcastic nod to their tactics, but the experience soured what could have been a unique dining adventure. The food had flashes of brilliance, but the lack of integrity in service overshadowed it. For a place that prides itself on being “unusual,” it’s ironic that their ethics feel so predictably shady. I’ll likely avoid returning—despite the pakoras—because trust, once dented, doesn’t come back. Way to go indeed.

The rest of the evening was a total bust. We missed half the movie scrambling to resolve the chaos, and honestly, the stress ruined any chance of enjoying the Breaking Dawn marathon. The Twilight saga was always a dramatic ride, but this theater mishap? That’s the real vampire drama. I get movies need a certain vibe, but this manager’s over-the-top antics felt like a horror film of its own. Who takes a complaint about "harassment" seriously when the victims never even *entered* the bathroom? It’s wild how one overzealous employee can tank an entire experience.  

Still, I’ll admit: the staff here isn’t all terrible. The assistant manager—sweet, calm, and clearly sane—saved the day by redirecting us to a private screening room for the remainder of the marathon. She even brought us popcorn and apologized for the nightmare. That kindness kinda made up for the trauma, but honestly? It shouldn’t take a customer’s mom screaming at a man to fix things.  

If you’re heading to this Harkins location, *please* avoid the bald, 5’5” manager at all costs. I’m not joking—he looked like a character from a slasher film, and his idea of “theater etiquette” is a joke. I’ve been to cleaner restrooms in public bathrooms at gas stations. The irony? This is the only Harkins near my house, so I still come back for the convenience, but I’ll never *relax* here again. Just keep your whispers soft, your snacks quiet, and your distance from management. And if you spot that guy? Leg it. Trust me.  

All in all, Harkins can still be a decent spot for a movie night—if you ignore the fact that I once had to fight to *not* be falsely accused of a crime while watching Bella get turned into a vampire. Priorities, people.

continued review:  
...go-to spot! The staff’s attentiveness made our celebration special, and the portions were generous without the all-you-can-eat option. We’ll definitely return for the creative dishes and warm vibe. Special shoutout to the team for making our daughter feel celebrated—this place has earned a loyal fan in our family!  

(74 words)

The lackluster service significantly diminished the otherwise pleasant aspects. While the menu offered solid, flavorful fare like crispy fries and hearty sliders, the bartender’s disengagement made the experience feel rushed. The dim lighting and muted music added to the laid-back vibe, but without attentive staff, it felt more neglected than cozy. Management’s friendliness couldn’t compensate for the apathy. Still, it’s a decent spot for a quick, affordable bite if you’re willing to overlook the lack of warmth. I’d return for the food but not the ambiance or service.

The only good thing about this place is the ice cream, which is creamy and richly flavored. Beyond that, the chaos reigns: staff overwhelmed by the all-you-can-eat menu rushed through tasks, leaving tables ignored. My repeated drink orders were met with empty promises, and even the “abundant” food felt overpriced and uninspired. Between the neglect and the steep costs, the experience felt transactional, not enjoyable. Save your money for better-reviewed spots where service and value matter.

The menu’s reliance on bold spices and tender meats like tandoori chicken and seekh kebabs is a saving grace, with each bite bursting with smoky, well-balanced flavors. However, the vegetarian options—like dry dal or under-seasoned aloo mutter—feel like afterthoughts, bereft of the depth or creativity seen in the meat dishes. The naan, though consistently soft and charred to perfection, often comes with a side of greasy garlic butter that overshadows its quality. While the affordability (plates under $10) is tempting, the lack of attention to basics—like fresh water or attentive service—dulls the experience. The staff’s indifference to wiping down sticky tables or clearing crumbs from seats adds to the frustration. Still, for those prioritizing hearty, flavorful meats over ambiance or punctuality, this place delivers. Just be prepared to leave a tip for cleaning your own table.

Continuing the review: The in-laws were equally impressed, especially with the restaurant’s warm, vibrant atmosphere—colorful décor that feels like a lively celebration of Mexican culture without leaning too heavily into cliché. Our server, a knowledgeable local, offered great recommendations, including the *enchiladas verdes* topped with tangy tomatillo sauce, which became a new favorite for my husband. While the menu leans heavily on traditional flavors, the shrimp *cemitas* (a house twist on a classic Mexican sandwich) stood out for its crusty bread and fresh cilantro-lime slaw. We also appreciated the generous portions—nothing felt skimpy or overpriced. If we had one critique, it’s that the queso fundido, while rich, occasionally veered into greasy territory. Still, the consistency across visits and the way the food makes you crave seconds (or thirds) speaks volumes. From the lively mariachi playlist to the attentive staff, Eldorado Grill feels like a neighborhood gem that’s earned its reputation. Whether you’re a spice enthusiast or a fan of avocado-forward dishes, this place has something to satisfy—and a margarita that’ll make you want to stick around for dessert.

The staff was attentive and friendly, adding to the warm, welcoming vibe. I also tried their avocado toast with a poached egg, which was creamy and well-balanced. The menu offers creative twists on classics, like the house-made sourdough and seasonal toppings. While the portions are modest, the emphasis on quality over quantity shines through—every bite felt intentional. The outdoor seating area, shaded by string lights, is perfect for morning brunch dates. For lunch, the quiche options are rich but not overwhelming, paired with a house-made herb salad. I appreciated the absence of artificial flavors; everything felt farm-fresh. Though the price point is slightly higher, the experience justifies it. I’ll definitely return to explore their weekend specials. A gem for those craving hearty yet refined comfort food.

The mall boasts a sleek, modern design with an open-air courtyard that feels inviting. While it lacks the sprawling size of mega-malls, its curated selection of luxury brands like Louis Vuitton, Gucci, and Rolex ensures a high-end experience without the overcrowding. The attached Grand Canal Shops add convenience, allowing shoppers to seamlessly blend retail therapy with a scenic stroll along waterways. Dining options are limited but upscale, ideal for post-shopping indulgence. Though modest, it’s perfect for those seeking a relaxed, premium shopping trip—especially after a lucky slot win! (79 words)

The staff’s apathy is staggering. I waited 15 minutes for help, only to be brushed off while they rushed to assist others. The jewelry consultants didn’t even check stock or offer alternatives. For a brand that prides itself on service, this neglect is disappointing. Neiman’s may lack your selection, but their attentiveness is unmatched. Save your “Nordy” charm for stores that prioritize customers over speed.

The atmosphere has a cozy retro vibe, feeling like a hidden gem. Regulars foster a welcoming community, and the juiciest burgers, crisp wings, and classic cocktails with a twist are consistently solid. Live music on weekends adds charm without noise. Bartenders know your name and order, making every visit feel personal. Close to home, it’s easy to pop in after work for a no-frills unwind. Perfect for escaping the hustle while enjoying friendly, familiar faces and drinks that hit just right. (77 words)

The ambiance was cozy, with a casual vibe that suited our weekend brunch plans. Our waitress was attentive and cheerful, making up for the lackluster menu options with friendly recommendations and prompt refills. The standout moment was watching the chef crack eggs with a theatrical flair and engage in lighthearted banter with diners—his energy added a fun touch to the meal. While the portions were generous (even the “mini” bagels felt ample), the waffles’ sogginess was a minor disappointment. We also noted that the syrup selection was limited, but the peaches’ sweetness compensated. Drinks were a highlight: the frozen mimosas were refreshing and perfectly balanced, though the orange juice could’ve used more tang. For $35, it’s a decent splurge, especially if you prioritize service and atmosphere over culinary innovation. It’s not a destination for die-hard foodies, but as a laid-back spot for a fun brunch with good drinks and a side of humor, we’d return—especially for the chef’s performances. (143 words)

The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, with a casual vibe that makes it perfect for both solo visits or hanging with friends. The extensive beer menu includes craft brews, local favorites, and seasonal specials, ensuring there’s something for every palate. Portions are generous, and the attention to detail—like housemade sauces and a commitment to quality—sets this place apart. Whether you’re a meat lover or prefer plant-based options, the menu caters to all without compromise. It’s a gem that feels like a neighborhood staple, and I’d highly recommend making it a must-visit for any burger and beer enthusiast. The only downside? You’ll probably need to save room for dessert—trust me, the banana pudding is worth it. (90 words)

The response from JJ was not only prompt but deeply sincere, which made me feel genuinely valued as a customer. I admired that the owner took personal responsibility rather than deflecting the issue, and the gesture of offering a free drink was a lovely way to rebuild trust. When I returned to Grouchy John’s last week, I was thrilled to meet both JJ and John in person—they greeted me warmly, ensured my drink was flawless, and even gifted a pastry with a smile. Their dedication to customer satisfaction is evident, and it’s clear this team prioritizes care over just coffee. The improved experience, paired with their transparency, has turned a potential negative into a story of hospitality that’s hard to find these days. I’ll definitely be back, and I’ll enthusiastically recommend their shop to anyone seeking great coffee—and a business that listens.

After the exchange, the "firmest" comfort layer still left much to be desired—it was only moderately firm, not the robust support we expected. My husband and I again felt our backs aching within days, reinforcing that the product didn’t align with its advertised firmness levels. To make matters worse, the replacement layers arrived with visible flaws: one was discolored, and another had what looked like fabric snags and dust buildup. I documented the damage and sent multiple follow-ups to the sales manager, but our concerns were met with radio silence.  

The entire experience was frustrating and disheartening. We were already skeptical about buying a mattress online, but this company’s lack of transparency, inconsistent product quality, and unresponsive customer service sealed the deal. While the refund for the initial charge was partial, the hassle of dealing with returns and the physical toll of an unsuitable mattress made the process exhausting. I regret the decision and can’t recommend Mattress Underground. Save yourself the time and money—prioritize brands with physical showrooms or lenient return policies.

The fro-yo itself is still a treat, but the staff’s unhelpfulness overshadows the experience. On my second visit, they refused to let me try a new flavor, claiming “no samples today” despite the sign saying otherwise. It’s disheartening when employees treat customers as if we’re committing a crime by simply exploring options. Other locations should check in on this store—basic hospitality is missing. For now, I’ll stick to places where the service matches the quality of the product. (66 words)

Here’s the continuation of the review (312 words):  

The contrast between the stunning view and the subpar execution of the meal was jarring. While the restaurant’s location at the Phoenix Sky Harbor area offers a panoramic vista of the Sonoran Desert and city lights, it felt like the kitchen fell short of the same level of polish. The Lobster Bisque and salad were bright spots, with the bisque’s rich, velvety texture and the salad’s crisp, tangy balance hinting at what the meal could have been. Unfortunately, the main course derailed the experience entirely. My wife’s scallops were a textbook case of mismanagement: the charred exterior suggested a rushed sear, while the cold center betrayed a lack of attention to temperature control. The overseasoning overwhelmed any delicate flavor the dish might have had, and the portions, while artfully plated, felt stingy for their $32 price tag.  

The service added to the frustration. After the waiter failed to check in, the Maitre d’s erroneous wine suggestion was an unnecessary stumble. Though the Merlot I selected was a decent palate cleanser, the lack of support for a clearly problematic dish underscored a disconnect between front-of-house and kitchen. For a special occasion, this oversight felt like a breach of trust. Even the absence of background music—the one odd note in an otherwise serene setting—seemed to amplify the awkward silence as we silently navigated the meal.  

Despite the kitchen’s failure, the wine list itself was a minor bright spot. Their cellar boasts a curated selection of regional and international wines, many reasonably priced by Phoenix standards. However, the experience left a bitter aftertaste, literally and figuratively. The review’s title, *“

The staff’s dismissive attitude only deepened the disaster. When we mentioned the salted burger patty, our server shrugged and said, “It’s a *seasoned* beef blend.” *Seasoned* meaning “drenched” in sodium, apparently. The salad? A crime scene of wilted lettuce and rubbery croutons, drowning in a vinegar-drenched dressing that tasted like regret. Even the fries—priced at a premium—were undercooked and leaden, though at least they didn’t taste like table salt. The bill, however, was staggering for food this calamitous. We split it, but only because pooling money for an ambulance felt more practical. The atmosphere didn’t help; flickering lights and a smell like burnt hair made it feel like dining in a derelict tavern. This isn’t a restaurant—it’s a public health hazard. Save your appetite, your wallet, and maybe your blood pressure. If this place had a rating below one star, they’d deserve it.

The service was friendly and prompt, which helped elevate the experience slightly. While the steakhouse’s décor felt dated in some areas, the bar had a modern, chic vibe that we appreciated. Unfortunately, the lackluster dishes were hard to overlook—the "garbage salad" (a clever twist on a classic) and creamy mac and cheese were the only highlights. The rest of our meal felt uninspired, with flavors that lacked depth. For the price, we expected more creativity and attention to detail. Still, the convenient location and decent wine list might convince us to give it another shot, though we’ll likely stick to the hotel’s other, more reliable spots.

The staff is on a HUGE power trip! They treated us like we were asking for the moon, while their "policy" excuses rang hollow. My guest was humiliated, and our celebration turned into a farce. We arrived late, exhausted, only to face more attitude and delays. The manager offered zero apology or compensation. Save yourself the stress and heartache—this place prioritizes ego over customer care. Our guest deserves better, and so do you! Don’t waste your time on their unnecessary games. (Word count: 89)

Let me paint the picture. We are obsessed with our Chihuahua. When I say obsessed—*I mean we have had a painting commissioned after him*. A typical Saturday is centered around him. **HE WALKED DOWN THE AISLE AT OUR WEDDING**. We are obsessed.  

We decided to change our vet due to their prices steadily increasing to the point that we could no longer justify going there.  

Our amazing, perfect Chihuahua ended up having a series of problems. We also brought in our other Chihuahua who can be a demon dog and attack.  

1. **Oona was INCREDIBLE with the demon dog.** Not one problem. This dog is known for being evil. He loves Oona. You have to be confident and firm with him. She handled him like a pro, even when he snarled and bared his teeth, and her calm demeanor diffused the tension. She didn’t treat him like a “problem” but instead as a misunderstood animal.  

2. The amazing Chihuahua is deaf and difficult to calm. I felt horrible. Oona knows our obsession with this dog and saw some possible problems. She wasn’t able to help him—*but referred him to another clinic*. I LOVE THAT OONA DID THAT. She was able to say “I can’t help with this—try these people,

The bar menu also had a decent selection of brews on tap, with a few local favorites that made the priciness a bit easier to swallow. The happy hour specials (5 PM–7 PM) were a saving grace, offering $5 off drafts and $3 off most appetizers. We split a plate of the aforementioned poppers and a round of discounted drinks, which felt like a better deal than ordering entrees. However, the main courses left much to be desired. The chicken and waffles were under-seasoned, and the ribs—though fall-off-the-bone tender—tasted like they’d been sitting in the steam table for hours. My partner’s fish and chips were soggy, and the fries seemed more like store-bought frozen than hand-cut.  

The atmosphere, while lively, felt cramped during peak hours, with tables wedged so close together that we could hear neighboring conversations mid-sentence. That said, the jukebox was a nice touch, and the retro sports memorabilia on the walls added character.  

While I’d return for a casual drinks-and-snacks vibe, I’d skip the entrées next time. The Hurricane is fine for a quick, no-frills hangout but lacks the polish to justify its inflated prices. If you’re in the mood to splurge on better bites, there are plenty of neighboring spots that deliver more value for your dollar. Still, with a friendly staff and a few solid starters, it’s not a complete bust—just don’t expect magic.

The Min Lu family’s track record with their Chandler location is impressive—consistent quality, diverse cuisine, and a warm, family-friendly vibe. Their buffet there offers everything from steaming seafood towers to hand-pulled noodles and made-to-order dim sum, all at a reasonable price. I’m hopeful their new location will bring back the charm and variety that made the original Hometown Buffet a gem. Let’s face it, the previous iterations—like City Buffet’s confusing “cook-your-own” gimmicks—felt forced and undermined the buffet’s soul. With Min Lu’s focus on fresh, authentic flavors and a welcoming atmosphere, this new chapter could be just what the neighborhood needs. I’m already imagining the smells of sizzling woks, the clamor of happy diners, and the joy of unlimited mango sticky rice. Fingers crossed they revive the magic! Can’t wait to dig in this Spring! 🍽️✨

The BTG menu features a curated selection of Old World and New World bottles, with some hidden gems that elevate the dining experience for wine enthusiasts. The Houston Roll, a spicy tuna creation with a delightful crunch, remains a standout—consistent and flavorful. While friends haven’t been overly wowed, they’ve always left content, which I chalk up to solid, no-fuss execution. Now that my 2-year-old joins me, the straightforward vibe and predictable menu are a win. No pretension, just reliable food and wine pairings. My kid loves the simplicity (and the sweet rice), and I appreciate the calm, low-stakes outings. It’s a happy middle ground where I’m comfortable and even a little proud to share sushi with my tiny critic. Worth the repeat visits.  

(91 words)

The turkey Cuban was a flavor-packed masterpiece—crispy pickles, smoky turkey, and that tangy Creole mustard blended perfectly. The red beans and rice, rich with Andouille, were a comforting, soul-warming side. The fast, friendly service made it easy to enjoy lunch without missing conference sessions. While Columbus lacks NOLA’s vibe, this spot nailed the authentic taste and generosity of New Orleans. Every bite felt like a mini-vacation. The portions are worth sharing, but honestly, I’d eat the whole thing solo. A top recommendation for any pit stop in the Market District! (82 words)

Continued review:  

The lack of a program or any context left me feeling adrift—Cirque’s shows often lean on visual storytelling, but without even a basic synopsis, it’s hard to connect emotionally. I kept waiting for a moment that would tie the chaos together, but it never came. That said, the technical aspects were undeniably masterful. The stage’s seamless transitions between levels and rotating sections created a sense of endless possibility, making the theater feel far larger than it was. It’s a feat of engineering that deserves its own standing ovation.  

The costumes were another highlight—vivid, intricate, and seemingly weightless, even during the most frenetic acrobatics. The music, a mix of haunting melodies and pulsating rhythms, amplified the drama without overpowering the action. Yet, for all the spectacle, the live audience experience felt oddly detached. The theater’s acoustics muffled some moments, and the lighting, while dramatic, sometimes obscured facial expressions. It’s a shame, because the performers’ physical storytelling (like the heartwarming hand-shadow sequence) hinted at deeper themes that never fully landed.  

If you’re booking last-minute and prioritize visuals over narrative, this could still be worth it—for the stage alone. But pay full price without context? I’m not sure. Still, I’ll admit: I’m already curious to see how the same stage transforms for future shows. Just bring a program next time, Cirque. You’d convert more skeptics.

The room was clean with basic amenities, and the location is convenient for exploring the Strip. While the service was friendly, it lacks the upscale features and luxury of top-tier hotels like the Venetian. A solid pick for budget-conscious travelers seeking a no-frills, affordable stay in Vegas.

The menu is disappointingly limited, offering just a handful of standard burger options without any flair or creativity. Even the fries, which are often a saving grace for average burgers, were under-seasoned and stale. For a place that positions itself as a burger haven, the absence of even basic upgrades like jalapeños, bacon, or creative sauces feels like an oversight. The staff seemed disengaged, and the bar crowd appeared more interested in the drinks than the food, which further muddled the overall experience. While the ambiance and bar might appeal to those prioritizing cocktails over cuisine, I left wondering how this place consistently draws praise. At nearly $10 for a forgettable burger and $20 for a “premium” version with mediocre toppings, it’s hard to justify the price tag—especially when far superior, budget-friendly alternatives exist elsewhere. This spot might be a safe bet for a drink, but if you’re craving a memorable burger, you’d be better off skipping the wait and heading to your favorite local diner instead.

Le décor est moderne et chaleureux, parfait pour un repas rapide ou en famille. La poutine est crémeuse et bien gratinée, un must ! Leur hot-dog avec macaroni au fromage est déroutant mais réussi. À noter : les portions généreuses sans prise de tête. Les prix restent abordables (moins de 10 $ pour tout repas). Cinko devient mon arrêt préféré en semaine, surtout quand j’ai envie de quelque chose de bien québécois et pas ringard ! Idéal aussi pour un apéro sympa entre amis sans se ruiner. À recommander sans hésiter !  

(Word count: 92)

The experience left me with a mix of appreciation and mild disappointment. While the single staff member’s efficiency and warmth were commendable, the lack of a team made me worry about how he managed during busier hours. The decor, though sparse, had a few endearing touches—a small Korean flag, a framed photo of a traditional market, and a rack of tea leaves—hints of culture that added character without overwhelming the space.  

The food’s inconsistency was a letdown. The ddukbokki’s sogginess and muted spice felt like a missed opportunity, as rice cakes are usually a highlight of Korean cuisine. The kimchi fried rice, however, was a standout: the rice was perfectly crisped, and the umami from the fermented kimchi balanced the soy sauce’s saltiness. The yukgaeyang was hearty but forgettable, its broth simple and the beef slightly overcooked.  

What stood out most was the value. For the prices listed (around $12-$15 per dish), the portions were generous, and the staff’s attentiveness made up for the kitchen’s shortcomings. While this isn’t a place to seek Michelin-starred finesse, it’s a solid option for casual Korean comfort in a town with few alternatives. If you’re craving a quick, no-frills meal where the rice is always satisfying, it’ll do the trick. But if you’re after bold flavors or an array of banchan to dive into, you might leave yearning for the bustling energy and variety of home.

The rest of the meal was equally lackluster—cold fries, over-seasoned sides, and a burger so bland it felt like a waste. Paying for "gourmet" here is a scam. My stomach’s still recovering, and regretfully, this was my final straw. Save your money and appetite; there’s no redeeming this experience. Skip the "micro burger" entirely—it’s an insult to the name. Never again.

The laid-back vibe makes it perfect for unwinding after a day of Vegas excitement. Staff is friendly and efficient, though service isn’t five-star. The island-inspired décor and outdoor seating add charm, but it’s straightforward without frills. Food hits the spot for casual meals, with fresh seafood and tropical twists. Located slightly off the Strip, it’s a peaceful retreat. Ideal for travelers prioritizing comfort over luxury, this spot delivers value for a stress-free, no-fuss stay.

The Chicken and Waffles were perfectly crispy, with a sweet-and-spicy kick that balanced the tender, juicy chicken. The Muddy Water drink was refreshing and added a fun twist to the meal. The staff’s warmth and attentiveness made us feel welcome, and the free banana pudding—a creamy, cinnamon-dusted dream—was the cherry on top. Between the stellar food, friendly vibe, and proximity to home, it’s a no-brainer for repeat visits. Their weekly specials (like the smoked salmon Benedict I glimpsed) have me excited for next time. Can’t wait to bring friends!  

(88 words)

The overpriced menu boasts "artisanal" bites that taste like cafeteria leftovers, while the forced "vibe" screams desperation. Bartenders shuffled like robots, and the playlist? A cringe-worthy mix of hipster clichés. Save your cash and skip the fake farm-to-table facade—this "scene" is a ghost town in disguise. Don’t waste your time.

The atmosphere was casual but cramped, with a slight odor from the open kitchen. We ordered lemonade, which was watered down, and shared a side of onion rings—okay, but nothing special. The staff was polite but overwhelmed, which I could understand given the rush. While the food quality was solid, the lack of a covered dining area made it uncomfortable during a sudden breeze. I’d recommend ordering the burger to-go next time, but for sit-down, it’s a gamble. Still, with a few tweaks—like better resting times, enclosed seating, and stronger drinks—this could be a top contender. For now, it’s a 3.5-star experience.

The main course, a perfectly seared filet mignon, was juicy and seasoned just right, paired with a rich red wine reduction that elevated the dish. Our waiter’s quirky jokes and animated storytelling added charm, turning a casual dinner into a memorable night. The ambient lighting and modern décor made the space feel lively yet intimate. As the fireworks lit up the sky, our group laughed and clinked glasses over the restaurant’s signature cocktail—a bourbon-spiked old fashioned that balanced sweetness and depth. Between the flawless execution of every detail and the unexpected magic of the fireworks, it’s no wonder we’re already planning our next visit. This place isn’t just a meal; it’s an experience. Two thumbs up!

The ambiance of the restaurant certainly added to the allure—we loved the modern, art-filled decor and the soft lighting that made the space feel intimate yet lively. The wait staff’s attentiveness was a bright spot; our server checked in frequently, refilled drinks without hesitation, and seemed genuinely invested in ensuring we enjoyed our meal. Still, the contrast between the stellar service and the hit-or-miss food left us conflicted. While the tableside mozzarella preparation was a fun, theatrical experience, the overly dry short ribs and undercooked steak felt like missteps in execution. It’s hard to ignore when the main courses don’t meet basic expectations, especially at a place where presentation clearly matters.  

The decision to forgo a replacement steak for my wife’s meal highlighted the pressures of timing—dining before a movie means you’re racing against a schedule, and waiting for corrections can feel impractical. However, the dessert, described as “Red Velvet Bread Pudding,” was a disappointment. It lacked the warmth and spice we associate with red velvet, tasting overly milky and underseasoned. Even the best service couldn’t salvage that final bite.  

While the restaurant isn’t without charm, the inconsistencies were hard to overlook. For the price point, we expected more consistency in both cooking and flavor profiles. There are so many other solid options nearby, from cozy bistros to upscale steakhouses, that make this spot feel less compelling. We’ll likely pass on another visit unless we’re curious about their weekend brunch (rumor has it their pancakes are a local favorite). For now, we’re saving our enthusiasm for places where the food matches the ambition of the design and service.

The menu remained disappointingly uninspired, with the same old pub fare that fails to elevate Rock Bottom beyond a generic beer hall. I ordered the pretzel bites, which were warm and pretzel-shaped, but flavorless and paired with a forgettable mustard. The fries were greasy, and the burger—priced at $18—was a limp patty drowned in a pool of ketchup, with no discernible toppings. For the cost, you’d expect something that might justify the meal, not just filler to keep the table occupied while waiting for drinks.  

The bar’s indifference reached a peak when one of us finally flagged down a bartender after ten minutes of waving. He snapped, “What?” before begrudgingly taking our order. When my beer arrived, it was lukewarm—a crime in any establishment that markets itself as a “brewpub.” Meanwhile, a group at the next table got immediate attention with a single raised hand. It felt less like a restaurant and more like a waiting room where your presence is only acknowledged when someone deigns to notice you.  

Rock Bottom’s location, while convenient for a downtown comedy show, becomes a liability for anything longer than a quick stop. By the time we left, drained by the effort of navigating the service and underwhelmed by everything else, I couldn’t help but think: if the beer were *exceptional*, maybe I’d forgive the rest. But good-to-adequate craft brews don’t justify subpar fries, a hostile staff, and a trek across town. Rock Bottom clings to the “nice” veneer of familiarity, but when the fundamentals of hospitality are this lacking, “nice” is just a euphemism for “meh.”

The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, with a touch of Southern charm that makes you feel right at home. Every bite of the shrimp felt like a celebration of flavor—the crispy, golden breading had a slight kick from what I can only guess is their homemade spice blend, and the house-made cocktail sauce, which had a tangy, garlicky richness, elevated the whole dish. The sides were equally impressive: the corn was tender and sweet, steamed to perfection, while the slaw was light yet packed with zing from a zesty dressing that balanced the crunch of fresh veggies.  

What really stands out is the authenticity. The menu feels rooted in tradition but with a creative twist, like the option to add spicy remoulade or hushpuppies to your meal. The staff’s passion for their food shines through in every interaction—they’re not just servers but storytellers, eager to share how the recipes were passed down through generations. With its community-focused vibe and top-notch food, this spot isn’t just a dining destination—it’s a local gem. Whether it’s a quick lunch or a weekend date night, this place checks all the boxes. Can’t recommend it enough!

The performers’ synergy was mesmerizing—each leap and spin felt like poetry in motion. The soundtrack, a mix of haunting melodies and pulsating rhythms, amplified the raw emotion in every scene. Even the lighting and set design wove into the magic, transforming the stage into a realm where reality blurred with imagination. I’d never seen an audience so collectively invested, gasping, cheering, and yes, still tearful. It was more than a show; it was a cathartic experience, a celebration of human connection and courage. The final bow left us buzzing, eager to debate the story’s meaning. I’ve recommended it to everyone—this is theater at its most transcendent. 104 words.

The continued frustration with the staff is only compounded by the store’s chaotic atmosphere. I’ve encountered similar rudeness in the home goods section, where an employee snapped at me for “hovering too long” near a display, as if my interest in products was a personal affront. It’s baffling—stores thrive on customer engagement, yet these employees seem determined to make shopping feel like an intrusion. Beyond the hostility, the disorganization feels deliberate. Last week, I spent 20 minutes searching for the cleaning supplies aisle, only to find it barricaded by stacked boxes. When I finally located it, half the shelves were empty, and the remaining products were crammed haphazardly. It’s clear management doesn’t prioritize customer experience.  

The lack of basic upkeep is equally maddening. Worn-out signage, broken floor tiles, and lingering food smells from the adjacent kitchen section create an uninviting environment. Even the “sales” events feel like a slapdash effort to draw in shoppers, since the items on discount are often buried under clutter or mislabeled. I’ve walked out more than once, defeated by the stress of navigating this minefield.  

While the occasional deal is tempting, the cumulative effect of the employees’ hostility and the store’s squalor is untenable. Every visit feels like a gamble—will I endure another “hmmph,” another obstacle course of furniture, or another moment where my patience is tested for no reason? I’m willing to overlook minor inconveniences, but this is negligence. Until there’s real investment in staff training and store organization, I’ll keep my business elsewhere—even if it means missing out on the good prices. After all, what’s a bargain if you have to battle an army of disgruntled employees and a junkyard layout to claim it?

The service, however, was inconsistent—our waitress often vanished, forcing us to flag down others for help. While the sushi and tempura were fresh and flavorful, the disjointed experience left a sour note. We’ll likely stick to takeout next time to avoid the frustration, but the food’s quality alone might tempt us to give the dine-in experience another shot if service improves.

The potato skins, honestly, were the only saving grace. Crispy on the outside with a gooey, cheesy center, they were a small burst of joy in an otherwise chaotic meal. But beyond that, the kitchen errors and lack of service were hard to overlook. We flagged a server multiple times for drinks refills and payment—each time, it took 10+ minutes just to get a response. The manager never acknowledged the overcooked steaks or the fact that we had to eat sizzling, unseasoned sides while waiting for anything else. For the price, you expect a baseline of competence. Instead, we got a scramble where everyone felt like an afterthought. If the potato skins were a full menu item and the rest of the meal didn’t exist, this place might earn three stars. As it stands, the positives are too minor to justify the frustration. I’ll stick with two stars, but I won’t be returning. Save your money and appetite for a place that actually respects its customers.

The only saving grace at Tin Tin is the crab legs, which my parents insist are worth the trip. But even that feels like a stretch when the rest of the meal is so underwhelming. The saltiness isn’t just a minor issue—it’s a consistent flaw across almost every dish. I tried the Mongolian beef, which should be a dish I’d enjoy, but it was so oversalted it bordered on inedible. The sweet-and-sour pork? Overly sugary in an unbalanced way that left my teeth feeling coated in syrup. Even the vegetables, which are usually a safe bet, were drowning in soy and sodium.  

The sushi selection, while small, was equally disappointing. The rice was bland, the fish lacked freshness, and the rolls felt more like a afterthought than a specialty. For a buffet priding itself on variety, there’s a staggering lack of depth. The fruit bar was an eyesore—melons that were mealy, berries that had clearly been sitting for hours, and tropical fruits that tasted like they’d been stored in a warehouse. And don’t even get me started on the dessert. The ice cream, which we all inevitably go for to end the meal, is a generic, mass-produced flavor with a $5 price tag that feels like the final insult.  

While the space is undeniably stylish—modern with vibrant colors and open layouts—it’s hard to ignore how the food fails to meet even basic expectations. For a place that draws in repeat customers (or, in our case, family obligations), Tin Tin feels like it’s coasting on nostalgia rather than quality. If my parents were open to trying newer spots with fresher, more balanced flavors, this wouldn’t be a yearly letdown. But until then, we’ll keep going back to a place that seems content with mediocrity.

The first half dragged with lackluster performances and forced humor. While the final act had a few clever moments and tighter pacing, it couldn’t redeem the tedious earlier segments. A missed opportunity for engagement—only worth watching if you stick around for the brief, redeeming finale. Overall, a forgettable experience with inconsistent quality. (62 words)

The service was friendly and efficient both times I visited, which added to the positive experience. The menu had a few creative options beyond the turkey burger, like salads and grain bowls, but I was drawn to the same meal each visit to test consistency. While the turkey patty stayed flavorful and fresh, the fries remained a minor letdown—neither soggy nor overly greasy, but lukewarm. I appreciate the focus on fresh, wholesome ingredients, and the portions felt generous for the price. The interior was modern and bright, making it a pleasant spot for a quick lunch. Though the cost felt slightly high for a workday meal, the quality and cleanliness justify it for a occasional treat. I’d return for the turkey burger but hope the fries (and maybe a warm drink) get a little more attention next time.

"Each dish showcased artful precision, from velvety foie gras to perfectly timed coq au vin. The sommelier’s expertise shone through stellar pairings, while staff warmth made us feel celebrated. A transcendent dining experience—Vegas at its culinary finest!"  

(Word count: 36)

The continued review:  

Dessert was a must—how could we resist the “Death by Chocolate” plate they slid over like a guilty pleasure? Rich, fudgy layers with a molten center, paired with a scoop of salted caramel ice cream that somehow balanced the intensity. My dad, who usually sticks to apple pie, actually asked for a second bite of the Irish coffee cake (a St. Paddy’s Day special). Bold move, Dad.  

Service stayed stellar throughout. Even with the chaos of the patio—let’s be real, it’s a warzone of clinking glasses, bike-handlebar real estate, and the guy who thinks *yelling* into his phone is a conversation—the servers moved like synchronized swimmers. My waitress, Bonnie (yes, *my* Bonnie), checked in without being overbearing and didn’t judge my dad’s “just describe it to me, honey” approach to ordering. Kudos for patience.  

Now, a PSA: If you value your sanity, avoid peak hours. We arrived right when the lunch rush met the “let’s celebrate everything with green beer” crowd. The acoustics? A symphony of overlapping chatter and that one guy who insists “Whiskey in the Jar” is an acceptable karaoke choice. Still, there’s something charming about the chaos—it feels *alive*, even if your date’s “romantic” dinner turns into a shouting match about the specials board.  

As for the food, let’s just say I’ll forgive the parking trauma and bike-encroachment drama. The cali spinach salad? Still haunting my dreams in the best way. The corned beef? A revelation. My dad’s official stamp of approval? He’s already planning our next visit for his “hipster garlic bread day.”  

Sure, it’s not perfect. But who needs perfection when you’ve got a cafe that turns a parking fiasco into a story, a salad into a highlight reel, and a dad’s night out into a weirdly memorable victory lap? Bring cash for tips, a sense of humor, and maybe a helmet—if you’re biking here, seriously, *please* don’t park sideways.

Definitely recommend stopping in if you're a taco enthusiast. The carne asada was perfectly grilled and seasoned, while the El Pastor had a tangy, smoky flavor. Chile rellenos lacked wow factor but were decent. The slow pace added to the no-frills charm, and the staff was friendly despite the delays. Would return for the standout tacos, though I’d skip the chile rellenos. (62 words)

The menu offers a variety of fresh toppings, from zesty salsas to tender grilled chicken and hearty beans. Their customizable options cater to diverse tastes, ensuring each dish is tailored to your liking. While I’d love to see whole wheat tortillas, the overall quality, friendly service, and generous portions make this a standout choice for any meal. (57 words)

The McGriddle, in particular, is a disappointment—overfilled with syrup, undercooked, and often crumbling apart. Coffee is lukewarm, and even simple items like hash browns arrive soggy. While the staff is cheerful and efficient, the inconsistency is frustrating. For a quick bite, it’s passable, but if you’re craving anything more than basic fare, skip this spot. Save your appetite—and patience—for a better diner nearby. Curse you, McGriddle! (73 words)

The airport’s layout is intuitive, making it easy to navigate even during peak travel times. Southwest’s concourse is particularly efficient, with minimal wait times for boarding. For shopping, the mix of duty-free and local retailers is impressive, and the new food court offers diverse, quality options beyond the standard airport fare. If you’re pressed for time, the TSA is usually quick and orderly. Whether connecting flights or ending your journey, Phoenix Airport delivers a stress-free experience—reliable service, modern touches, and that rare combination of practicality and charm. Don’t miss the rooftop bar at the Sky Harbor Hotel either; the views of takeoffs are unforgettable.

The oriental buffet is a cut above most buffet. It is located just off of US60 and Country Club. I especially like their sushi selection. I can have a great meal just with sushi at a very reasonable price. I find their other selections ok as well. Ocean Buffet is definitely a place to stop by if you are in the area and hungry for oriental food. The staff is friendly, and the portions are generous. From fresh sashimi to flavorful tempura, every dish is made with care. Even the bento boxes and stir-fry options impress. At under $10, it’s a steal for quality and variety. Whether you’re a sushi connoisseur or just craving something different, this spot delivers consistent, satisfying flavors in a lively, no-frills setting. Don’t miss the daily specials—it’s what keeps me coming back! (67 words)

The prices have also spiked, making the lackluster offerings feel even less worth it. Service was sluggish, and our server seemed disinterested, neglecting to refill drinks. I attempted to order a signature roll, but it arrived bland and overpriced. The ambiance, once cozy, now feels cramped with dim lighting. While I understand evolution, this shift lost what made it special. If they can’t recapture their previous flair or justify the changes, I’ll stick to other local spots that prioritize quality and consistency.

Here’s the continuation of your review, staying true to the tone and expanding on the key points with a humorous yet critical voice:

The only "vibe" this place has going for it is the architectural audacity of its design. My room was sleek and modern, which I appreciate, but the minimalist aesthetic couldn’t compensate for the eerie silence. I half-expected a character from *The Shining* to pop out and hand me a drink. The worst part? The Wi-Fi. It was so spotty that my Zoom meetings with clients kept cutting out, and I resorted to pacing the hallway like a caffeinated maniac, hoping the signal would strengthen near the elevator. Spoiler: it didn’t.  

Speaking of the layout, let’s talk about the “hidden” features of this maze. The pool area is tucked behind a corridor labeled only in small, faded lettering. By the time I found it, I’d circled the hotel so many times I could’ve drawn a map blindfolded. The pool itself? A glorified kiddie wading pool with a lone lifeguard napping in a chair. I get it—the hotel’s trying to maintain its “exclusive retreat” energy—but a Jacuzzi or even a hot tub would’ve gone a long way. Instead, I was greeted by a sign reading “Hydro Massage Tub – Closed for Renovations” on day two.  

The staff’s lack of visibility became a running joke with my coworkers. One night, I waited 15 minutes for a housekeeper to unlock my door because the keycard wasn’t working. When I finally tracked someone down, they shrugged and said, “Maybe try the lobby desk?” as if the lobby *wasn’t* where

Upon arrival, we were bombarded with a high-pressure timeshare pitch disguised as a free breakfast offer. Lisa, the so-called customer service rep, misled us with false promises and later refused the $75 credit after claiming we left too soon. The 90-minute requirement was never mentioned upfront. The rooms are uncomfortably noisy, with thin walls and constant disturbances. Staff seemed uninterested in resolving complaints. This place prioritizes sales over guests. Save your money and avoid this scam at all costs!  

(81 words)

Haze can be summed up with one word. Maybe it's more of an onomatopoeia. Meh. The only reason we ended up here was because we had dinner at a restaurant in the Aria and we happened to follow a group of nice-looking ladies here.  

So why is Haze so meh you ask? Here's the breakdown:  

Decor: Less than stellar. I couldn't really pick up on any kind of theme and really, it just doesn't look that nice. In fact, it kind of just looks old and a bit run down. Isn't this one of the newer clubs in Vegas? The lighting felt dimmer to mask the dated design, and the furniture—uh, what furniture?—looked like it had seen better nights (and probably more disinfectant).  

Music: Not great, not bad, just okay. The DJs seemed to shuffle between generic top-40 hits and forgettable EDM drops. There was zero energy, like they were playing for a packed crowd instead of the sparse bunch that actually showed up. I half-expected someone to request *Yakety Sax* just to liven things up.  

Ambiance: The overall feel of the club felt a little off and disconnected. From the random elevated platforms in the middle of the dance floor to the professional dancers up on stage, I just wasn’t *feeling* it. Ya know? It was like they tried to cram a strip club vibe into a bar setting, and neither side won. Plus, the AC was either broken or set to “arctic,” making it uncomfortable to stand still.  

With that said, I did appreciate that the bouncers weren’t douche bags making people wait in line for no reason other than to create a line. I suppose I would come back here if I couldn’t find another place to go, but it definitely wouldn’t be my go-to spot and I definitely wouldn’t wait in a long ass line to get in. Bottom line: Haze is a forgettable experience. You’ll leave thinking, “Eh, could’ve been worse,” but also wondering why you spent your time (and $20 margarita)

The service was friendly, but the prices felt average for the lackluster experience. My bagel was under-seasoned and dense, leaving me hungry by mid-morning. While the pastrami had decent flavor, the mysterious sauce (a mix of sweet and vinegary notes) was an acquired taste. Both sandwiches felt like they prioritized quantity over quality—tiny bagels with minimal fillings. We’d return for the pastrami, but the menu needs more balance and better value. Would’ve loved a customizable order option without upsells. Definitely a “maybe” over “must-try.” (89 words)

The sound system is next-level immersive, making every scene feel like a front-row concert. The reclining seats, personal screens, and free snacks elevate the experience beyond a typical matinee. While the cost is daunting ($40+ for a ticket!), it’s easy to rationalize when you’re sipping craft cocktails at your seat. Scottsdale’s luxury theaters thrive on this “you pay, you get” model, and honestly? It works. After one session, regular theaters feel like a step back—rusty seats, cramped aisles, and that stale popcorn smell. I’ll save up for these tickets; some experiences are worth the splurge. Just don’t tell the regular theaters I said that… (95 words)

The lackluster atmosphere and overpriced games made it clear this was a shadow of its former self. Crane machines demanded three tokens for a slim chance at trinkets, while pinball’s dollar-per-play fee felt exploitative. The handful of functioning games—glitchy classics like *Ms. Pac-Man*—served as sad relics, their charm overshadowed by neglect. Families seemed disinterested, opting for nearby attractions instead. While the neon-lit design paid lip service to nostalgic grandeur, the emptiness and inflated costs rendered the experience transactional, not celebratory. Nostalgia alone can’t revive an arcade when the magic of communal play fades. Coney Island Emporium might cling to the past, but without revitalization, it’s just a hollow homage to an era it can’t recapture.

The prices are also surprisingly reasonable for the quality, making it feel like a real bargain. Even the simpler dishes, like their spring rolls or egg fried rice, are consistently satisfying. The portions are generous, and you never feel rushed, which is a rarity in busy spots. I’ve brought friends and family here countless times, and they always leave impressed. While the menu is solid overall, their dim sum selection (when available) is a hidden gem—fresh, flavorful, and worth the wait. Even though Ed isn’t around as much now, the newer staff are just as warm and eager to please. Whether you’re craving comfort food or something with a little culinary flair, this place delivers. It’s a local treasure, and I can’t imagine Phoenix without it. Keep up the great work! (113 words)

The baristas are knowledgeable, and the menu offers creative, locally sourced pastries. While the vibe is cozy, the occasional sideways glances from longtime patrons might make newcomers self-conscious, but the exceptional brew and warm service easily outweigh the subtle territorial energy. A solid choice for coffee purists.

The bathroom was no better—mold crept along the shower tiles, and the water pressure fluctuated between nonexistent and scalding. The staff, though apologetic, offered only perfunctory solutions, insisting the “stains” were “just fabric texture” and refusing to address the pervasive odor. Breakfast was a sad spread of lukewarm pastries and coffee that tasted like regret. I asked for Wi-Fi, only to learn the password required solving a riddle only the elevators could decode. Every interaction felt like a negotiation—extra towels? A hairdryer? A functioning desk lamp?—each request met with eye rolls and delays. The hotel’s website boasts “modern comfort,” but “modern” here means 1998: peeling wallpaper, flickering neon signs in the parking lot, and a front desk frozen in a time before smartphones. I left with a migraine, a suitcase of mildew memories, and zero desire to return. Save your money, your sanity, and your suitcase—this “hotel” is a masterclass in how *not* to travel. (146 words)
Portions are generous, and the freshness is undeniable. The wait is worth it—the chicken is juicy, and the catfish is crispy yet flaky. A cozy atmosphere completes the experience; highly recommend!

The stark contrast between our two visits left us deeply unsettled. The carefree, friendly service we experienced at breakfast was nowhere to be found during lunch. The server’s dismissive attitude—claiming she was “in a hurry” despite the empty restaurant—felt inconsiderate and unprofessional. Even more baffling was the meal itself. The catfish, touted as a highlight, arrived overpriced for its meager portions and heavy breading, which left it tasting more like breaded cardboard than fresh fish. The pairing of beef gravy with mashed potatoes alongside the catfish was not only jarring but offensive, given our dietary preferences. As vegetarians, the presence of meat-based gravy on our plate was a major oversight, compounded by the canned, flavorless veggies and a roll that crumbled at the touch.  

The final straw was the server’s lack of basic hygiene when she grabbed the fish with her bare hands, ignoring our request for a new plate. The owner, just a few feet away, failed to intervene, which raised serious concerns about management oversight. For a place that prides itself on hospitality, this experience felt tone-deaf and careless. While we’ll still recommend the breakfast for its warmth and quality, lunch here is a gamble. The inconsistencies in service, respect for dietary needs, and food preparation make it hard to justify returning. Stick to breakfast—or take a pass altogether.

**Continued Review:**  

Once the billing issue was resolved (which the team handled swiftly and with genuine apologies), I was free to focus on the rest of the experience—and wow, did it deliver! The limo itself was pristine, spacious, and equipped with everything you’d need for a night out. The music system was top-notch, and the drivers were clearly proud of the vehicle, pointing out cool features like the rotating ceiling and the mini bar (yes, really!). It felt like a VIP lounge on wheels, and my whole crew was in awe.  

What truly stood out, though, was the personal touch. The roses for the ladies were a sweet gesture, but the *champagne*—oh, the champagne! Two bottles before we even arrived at the club? That’s the kind of detail that makes a company memorable. And they didn’t stop there. When we called ahead to request an earlier pickup, they didn’t hesitate to adjust their schedule. Even though it meant the driver had to wait a bit, they prioritized our comfort, bringing an extra two bottles of bubbly to the second pickup. *Two more!* My group was *so* spoiled, and it didn’t feel like a paid service—it felt like we were friends.  

The drivers themselves were the cherry on top. Beyond being friendly, they were knowledgeable about Vegas and eager to help. When we mentioned wanting to grab a post-club bite, they suggested Fatburger (a local classic) and adjusted the route without any hassle. They even made small talk, asked about our trip, and made us feel like they *wanted* us to have the best night ever. That kind of attitude isn’t just good service—it’s rare.  

As for the nightclub access? Pure was packed that night, but we walked right in, skipped the line, and were handed wristbands that felt like golden tickets. The cover-free entry alone was worth it, but the real win was the time saved—not wasting hours waiting just to get in. My cousins were so impressed, and the group ended up staying until the club closed.  

The follow-up after the trip was equally stellar. Someone from the company emailed the next day to check in

Continued review: The ambiance of Local only added to the magic—cozy yet elegant, with just the right balance of chatter and soft music. The team’s ability to navigate a packed room without missing a beat spoke volumes about their expertise. We were especially impressed by the wine pairings Matthew suggested; the selections elevated every dish, including a bold Cabernet that complemented the pork ribs perfectly. Even the smallest touches, like the hand-written thank-you note from the chef tucked with our bill, felt deeply personal. Peg raved about the burrata’s creamy richness and the fig’s sweet contrast, while the duck risotto’s saffron depth lingered in our minds long after the meal. The pork tenderloin was cooked to textbook perfection—juicy, flavorful, and paired with polenta that had a lovely, silky finish. Our guests, who’d dined at Local before, agreed the lasagna was the best they’d had outside of Italy, and the ribs? Fall-off-the-bone spectacular. As for the tiramisu, it’s a masterpiece—decadent, refreshing, and the ideal cap to an already flawless evening. Whether it’s a quiet date night or a celebration, Local delivers a heartfelt, unpretentious experience that feels like a home-cooked meal with the flair of a five-star chef. Don’t hesitate—Local isn’t just a restaurant; it’s a neighborhood treasure. 185 words.
